struct_mappings.reason: Reach wraps a shader's body in a `render_method` struct under a 104-byte root that holds only that struct plus `material name`; Halo 4 puts the same body directly on the 68-byte `material` root. Halo 2 and earlier author a shader as a template reference plus a parameter/postprocess table (`template`, `parameters`, `postprocess definition`, `light response`, `specular type`, `lightmap type`); Halo 3 onward replaced that whole system with a render method. Measured: the two root structs share exactly one field name, `material name`, out of 16 and 2. A converted tag therefore carries a name and nothing else, and Guerilla rejects it as invalid. Reviewed: recreate the shader with the target engine's render-method system.

The other half of the pre-Halo 3 shader system. Halo 3 onward have no shader_template class; its role is served by render_method_template, which is authored differently. Reviewed: no field-level mapping is meaningful.

Halo 1 stores pixels big-endian in its own per-engine layout and its `bitmap_data_block` differs from every later generation's, so the blob cannot be carried straight into an MCC bitmap. Convert Halo 1 bitmaps to Halo 2 first (where the pixel blob does carry, byte for byte) and then forward. Reviewed: or re-import the source art with the target kit's tool.

A sound tag is a header for audio that lives somewhere else. The samples sit in per-engine banks — Halo 2 appends cache data past the structured body that no field references, Halo 3 onward use sound-gestalt resources and FSB banks — so nothing a field-level conversion can reach carries the audio. Converting one produces a header pointing at a bank the target game does not have. Reviewed against the author's own account of the format: sound tags should not be converted at all; re-import the source audio with the target kit's tool.

Reach onward removed `pixels offset` from `bitmap_data_block_def` entirely - the engine derives each bitmap's position in the shared blob from `four times log2 size` and friends instead - so a Halo 2 pixel blob carried straight there has nothing indexing it, which is what produced a bitmap whose metadata promised mipmaps with nothing behind it and crashed the Reach mod tools. Reviewed: convert to Halo 3 first, whose bitmaps do carry their pixels and already convert onward to Reach.

Halo 4 renamed contrail_system to tracer_system. Measured rather than assumed, because the catalog previously recorded the opposite: H3EK ships 67 contrail_systems and HREK 88 with no tracer_system between them, while H4EK ships 253 tracer_systems and none of the other. Both roots are a thin wrapper around one block of entries (`contrails`, `tracers`), and the entry structs share 21 of the contrail's 37 fields by name *and* type -- the whole substance of the effect: profile color, alpha, size, lifespan, rotation, rotation rate, offset, palette, shape, black point, intensity and self acceleration, plus uv scrolling and tiling, both fade pairs, appearance flags and sort bias. What differs is the known Halo 4 drift: `actual shader?` becomes `actual material?`, the entry's name field is renamed, and Halo 4 adds length, offset, density and angle fades while dropping emission rate and the per-entry lod distances. Those are reported per field, which is what a rename with feature drift should look like.

payload_aliases.reason: Both are the bitmap's pixel payload in the tag body under the same field name, `processed pixel data`; only the data definition was renamed. Verified against the kits rather than the schema: a native H3EK bitmap keeps 699,052 bytes in `processed pixel data` and populates no pageable resource at all, despite the schema marking the field `*` and declaring interop resources. The formats line up too - Halo 2's `format_enum_2` and Halo 3's `bitmap_formats` share both index and name for dxt1 (14), dxt3 (15), dxt5 (16) and every uncompressed entry, and the enum is carried by name in any case. Halo 2's `p8` and `p8-bump` have no Halo 3 option and are reported. Scoped to Halo 3 and ODST on purpose: Reach's `bitmap_data_block_def` has no `pixels offset` field at all, so a blob carried there would have nothing indexing it - go through Halo 3, whose bitmaps already convert to Reach.

accepted_payload_drops.reason: Sapien's own editor bookkeeping for the scenario, not gameplay data. Every profile declares it under the same field name and a different data definition (`editor_scenario_data_data` in Halo CE, `_data_3` in Halo 2's version-3 struct, `editor_scenario_data_definition` in Halo 3), so the opaque copy path has no identity to pair them on and refused the whole scenario over it. Measured: Halo CE ships it populated and Halo 2 ships it empty in every scenario its kit carries, which is what a per-editor scratch blob looks like. Reviewed as safe to drop -- one game's editor state means nothing to another's editor, and the scenario's actual contents live in the blocks around it.
